summary: Fang-Kuei Li worked in linguistics, sinology, and tibetology. Educated at Tsinghua, Michigan (BA), and Chicago (PhD under Edward Sapir, Leonard Bloomfield, and Carl Darling Buck), he held posts at Chicago, Academia Sinica, Yale, Harvard, Washington (1949–1969), and Hawaiʻi (1969–1974).
Faren studied buddhist and religious studies, completing a PhD at Lancaster University by 2008. Affiliation includes serving as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

A scholar in history and archaeology, Farzand Ali Durrani studied at the University of Peshawar, University of the Punjab, and University of London (~1959–1962). He served as professor at the University of Peshawar (attested 1990).
Fausta Nowotny was an Indologist who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1938–1942) under Erich Frauwallner. She worked as a staff member at the Weltmuseum Wien from 1943 to 1951.

Fausto Ghirardini Fumi specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying under Giuseppe Bardelli and at Pisa, Florence, and Leipzig. He taught at Liceo Classico Tommaso Campanella, the University of Palermo (1887–1890), and the University of Genoa (1890).

Fawad Khan works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, later serving as Assistant Curator at the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (attested 2022).

Fazun specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under teachers including Taixu, Dayong, Pabongka Dechen Nyingpo, and Amdo Geshe, and at Drepung Monastery. He served as director of the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies (1933) and president of the Buddhist Academy of China (1956).

Federica Venturi specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned her Ph.D. from Indiana University Bloomington (completed by 2013), where she also served as editor (attested 2004), and became an associate researcher at CRCAO in 2021.

Federico Squarcini works in Indology and religious studies. He became a professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 2011, served as series editor for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies (attested 2012), and joined the Marco Polo editorial board (attested 2022).

Felix Hartmann specialized in linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (1874–1880), under Jacob Wackernagel, and completing a Ph.D. at Göttingen (1881). He served as Oberlehrer at Preußische Hauptkadettenanstalt (1884) and docent at Berlin (1906–1935).

Felix Solmsen specialized in linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin under Johannes Schmidt and earning his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien. He served as Privatdozent (1893) and extraordinary professor (1897) at the University of Bonn.

Feng Youlan worked in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Central China Normal University, Peking University, Tsinghua University, and Columbia University. He held academic posts at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952), the University of Pennsylvania (1946–1947), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1946–1947).

Ferdinand Christian Baur worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen and Tübinger Stift (~1809–1814) and later served as a professor at the University of Tübingen from ~1826 to 1860.
Ferdinand Hahn worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Gossner Mission School in 1865 and served as a missionary with the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church beginning in 1869.

Ferdinand Hitzig worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829) and held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at Marburg and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Johann Gildemeister, and Heinrich Ewald. At Marburg, he became professor in 1865, full professor in 1869, and Rektor (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing worked in sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees at Berlin under F. W. K. Müller. He taught at Peking University, Berlin, and the Ethnological Museum of Berlin before serving as Agassiz Professor at UC Berkeley (1935–1949).

Ferdinand Masing was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu (1868–1869) and earned his PhD at the University of Leipzig (1874–1878) under August Leskien, Georg Curtius, Heinrich Hübschmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Karl Brugmann.

Ferdinand Sommer worked in linguistics and Indology, earning his doctorate at Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen and his Habilitation at Leipzig. He held professorships at Basel (1902), Rostock (1909–1913), Jena (1913–1924), Bonn (1924–1926), and Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied in Geneva, Berlin, and Leipzig (PhD under Ernst Windisch, Georg Curtius, Karl Brugmann, and August Leskien). He held posts at the EPHE (1881–1891) and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).
